subproblems.title: Lemma 3.2: rectifiable / purely unrectifiable decomposition
subproblems.statement:
For all n, ℓ ∈ ℕ and every A ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}, suppose there are A_j ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} (j ∈ ℕ) with A = ⋃_j A_j and Hⁿ(A_j) < ∞ for every j. Then:
(i) there are R, P ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with A = R ∪ P, R ∩ P = ∅, R countably n-rectifiable and P purely n-unrectifiable;
(ii) if moreover A is Hⁿ-measurable (NullMeasurableSet A μHE[n]), then there are such R, P with R in addition a Borel set.
Here Hⁿ = μHE[n] is applied as an outer measure.
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, Lemma 3.2 and its proof (chapter-03.txt lines 449-469, printed p. 78); parent proof Part 1, step 1.

Notation. ℝ^d = Rn d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d). Hⁿ = μHE[n], applied to arbitrary sets as an outer measure. CountablyRectifiable and PurelyUnrectifiable are the SimonGMT predicates opened by the contract.

Statement to prove (RectifiableDecomposition). For all n, ℓ and A ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}, assume there are A_j (j ∈ ℕ) with A = ⋃_j A_j and Hⁿ(A_j) < ∞ for all j. Then:
(i) ∃ R P, A = R ∪ P ∧ Disjoint R P ∧ CountablyRectifiable n R ∧ PurelyUnrectifiable n P;
(ii) if NullMeasurableSet A μHE[n], then ∃ R P, A = R ∪ P ∧ Disjoint R P ∧ MeasurableSet R ∧ CountablyRectifiable n R ∧ PurelyUnrectifiable n P.

Proof.

1. Fix n, ℓ, A and (A_j) as in the hypothesis. From A = ⋃_j A_j we get the cover A ⊆ ⋃_j A_j, and Hⁿ(A_j) < ∞ for every j.

2. Apply the kernel-checked theorem Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.simon_lemma_3_2 (Chapter03/Rectifiable.lean; this module is imported by the contract) with:
- E := ℝ^{n+ℓ}, the given n and the set A;
- the cover S := (A_j)_{j∈ℕ};
- hcover : A ⊆ ⋃_j A_j and hfinite : ∀ j, μHE[n] (A_j) < ∞.
Its first component is literally conclusion (i).
Its second component states: if NullMeasurableSet A μHE[n], then ∃ R P, A = R ∪ P ∧ Disjoint R P ∧ MeasurableSet R ∧ NullMeasurableSet P μHE[n] ∧ CountablyRectifiable n R ∧ PurelyUnrectifiable n P. Discarding the conjunct NullMeasurableSet P gives conclusion (ii).
The library lemma and the contract use the same objects CountablyRectifiable, PurelyUnrectifiable and μHE[n], so no translation is needed. This proves RectifiableDecomposition.

3. For completeness, here is the mathematics of the library proof. It is Simon lines 455-469, with Simon's α_j-supremum selection of closed sets R_ij replaced by an equivalent σ-finite exhaustion.
(a) σ-finiteness. Let B_j ⊇ A_j be Borel with Hⁿ(B_j) = Hⁿ(A_j) < ∞ (measurable hulls). Then A ⊆ ⋃_j B_j, so μ := Hⁿ⌞A is σ-finite.
(b) Exhaustion. Let C be the class of Borel, countably n-rectifiable subsets of ℝ^{n+ℓ}. C is closed under countable unions: interleave the countable families of Lipschitz maps via a pairing ℕ×ℕ → ℕ, and take the union of the Hⁿ-null exceptional sets. Since μ is σ-finite, there is a countable D ⊆ C such that μ(S ∖ ⋃D) = 0 for every S ∈ C (Mathlib Measure.exists_ae_subset_biUnion_countable). Put M := ⋃D; M is Borel and countably n-rectifiable.
(c) A ∖ M is purely n-unrectifiable. Let S ⊆ A ∖ M be countably n-rectifiable, say S ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_k F_k(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and F_k Lipschitz. Let B be the union of a Borel Hⁿ-null hull of M₀ with the sets F_k(ℝⁿ); these are σ-compact, hence Borel. Then B ∈ C and S ⊆ B. So μ(B ∖ M) = Hⁿ((B ∖ M) ∩ A) = 0, and S ⊆ (B ∖ M) ∩ A gives Hⁿ(S) = 0.
(d) For (i), take R := A ∩ M (countably rectifiable, being a subset of M) and P := A ∖ M.
(e) For (ii), suppose A is Hⁿ-measurable; then so is A ∩ M. Choose a Borel R ⊆ A ∩ M with Hⁿ((A ∩ M) ∖ R) = 0, and put P := A ∖ R. Then A = R ∪ P disjointly, R is Borel and countably rectifiable, and P ⊆ (A ∖ M) ∪ ((A ∩ M) ∖ R). Any countably rectifiable R' ⊆ P splits as R' ∩ (A ∖ M), which is Hⁿ-null by (c), and R' ∩ ((A ∩ M) ∖ R), which is Hⁿ-null. Hence P is purely n-unrectifiable. ∎
proof_key_steps: A = ⋃_j A_j gives the cover A ⊆ ⋃_j A_j with Hⁿ(A_j) < ∞.
SimonGMT simon_lemma_3_2 with S := (A_j) gives conclusion (i) directly. Its measurable part gives (ii) after dropping NullMeasurableSet P.
The library argument: σ-finite exhaustion by Borel countably rectifiable sets gives M; A ∖ M is purely unrectifiable; take R := A ∩ M, or a Borel inner approximation of it when A is Hⁿ-measurable.

subproblems.title: Some coordinate projection is injective on a given n-plane
subproblems.statement: For all N, n ∈ ℕ and every linear subspace L ⊆ ℝᴺ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) with dim L = n, there is a set J ⊆ Fin N with exactly n elements such that coordinateProjection J is injective on L. Here coordinateProjection J is the orthogonal projection of ℝᴺ onto span{e_j : j ∈ J}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (L : Submodule ℝ (Rn N)), finrank ℝ L = n → ∃ J : Finset (Fin N), J.card = n ∧ Set.InjOn (coordinateProjection J) (L : Set (Rn N))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 3.3, first claim (chapter-03.txt lines 482-489, printed pp. 78-79); parent proof Part 2, step 3.

Notation.
- ℝᴺ = Rn N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), with standard basis vectors e_j and j-th coordinate x_j of x.
- K_J := span{e_j : j ∈ J}.
- p_J := coordinateProjection J, by definition the orthogonal projection (Submodule.starProjection) of ℝᴺ onto K_J.

Statement. For all N, n and every subspace L ⊆ ℝᴺ with dim L = n, there is J ⊆ Fin N with #J = n such that p_J is injective on L.

Proof.

1. Coordinate formula. Let J ⊆ Fin N and x ∈ ℝᴺ, and put y := Σ_{j∈J} x_j e_j. So y_i = x_i for i ∈ J and y_i = 0 for i ∉ J.
Each e_j with j ∈ J lies in K_J, hence y ∈ K_J. For j ∈ J, ⟨x − y, e_j⟩ = x_j − y_j = 0. Every w ∈ K_J is a finite linear combination of such e_j, so ⟨x − y, w⟩ = 0 for all w ∈ K_J (induction on the span).
The orthogonal projection onto K_J is the unique v ∈ K_J with x − v ⊥ K_J (Mathlib Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero). Hence p_J x = y, that is:
(p_J x)_i = x_i if i ∈ J, and (p_J x)_i = 0 if i ∉ J.

2. The coordinate functionals span L*. For j ∈ Fin N, let φ_j ∈ L* be φ_j(x) := x_j for x ∈ L.
If x ∈ L and x ≠ 0, some coordinate x_j ≠ 0, i.e. φ_j(x) ≠ 0.
In a finite-dimensional space, a set of linear functionals that detects every nonzero vector spans the dual (Mathlib Submodule.span_eq_top_of_ne_zero). Indeed, suppose W := span{φ_j} ≠ L*. Then some nonzero functional on L* vanishes on W. Since L → L** is an isomorphism, that functional is evaluation at some x ∈ L with x ≠ 0, and φ_j(x) = 0 for all j — a contradiction.
So span{φ_j : j ∈ Fin N} = L*.

3. A basis of L* made of coordinate functionals. We have dim L* = dim L = n (Subspace.dual_finrank_eq). A spanning set of an n-dimensional space contains n linearly independent elements that span it (Mathlib Submodule.exists_fun_fin_finrank_span_eq, reindexed along finrank(span{φ_j}) = finrank L* = n by finCongr).
So there are j(1), …, j(n) ∈ Fin N such that φ_{j(1)}, …, φ_{j(n)} are linearly independent and span L*.
The indices are pairwise distinct: if j(a) = j(b), then φ_{j(a)} = φ_{j(b)}, and a linearly independent family is injective, so a = b.

4. The selected coordinates determine elements of L. Let z ∈ L with z_{j(i)} = 0 for i = 1, …, n. The functionals f ∈ L* with f(z) = 0 form a subspace containing every φ_{j(i)}, hence all of span{φ_{j(i)}} = L*. Since evaluation L → L** is injective, z = 0.

5. Put J := {j(1), …, j(n)}; by step 3, #J = n. Let x, x' ∈ L with p_J x = p_J x'. By step 1, x_{j(i)} = (p_J x)_{j(i)} = (p_J x')_{j(i)} = x'_{j(i)} for every i. Then z := x − x' ∈ L has z_{j(i)} = 0 for all i, so z = 0 by step 4, i.e. x = x'. Hence p_J is injective on L. ∎

Remarks.
(a) For n = 0 the argument works as written: L = 0, the family in step 3 is empty, and J = ∅.
(b) Simon's printed version: a matrix whose rows form a basis v_1, …, v_n of L has n linearly independent columns j₁ < ⋯ < jₙ (a nonsingular n × n minor), so p_J(v_1), …, p_J(v_n) are independent. Steps 2-4 are the dual form of this rank statement, as in the parent proof.
(c) SimonGMT Chapter03/CoordinateProjection.lean (exists_bijective_selectedCoordinateMap) contains steps 2-4. That module is not built in the pinned package and not imported by the contract, so the argument must be reproduced. It compiles with only import GMT.Ch03.Submission.
proof_key_steps: Coordinate formula: (p_J x)_i = x_i for i ∈ J and 0 otherwise, by the characterization of orthogonal projection.
The restricted coordinate functionals φ_j span L*, because a nonzero vector has a nonzero coordinate.
Extract coordinate functionals φ_{j(1)}, …, φ_{j(n)} forming a basis of L*; the indices j(i) are distinct.
A vector of L whose selected coordinates all vanish is 0.
J := {j(1), …, j(n)} has #J = n, and p_J is injective on L.

subproblems.title: C¹ maps on open sets send Lebesgue-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝⁿ be open, and let ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ be C¹ on V. If T ⊆ V has Lebesgue outer measure Lⁿ(T) = 0, then Hⁿ(ψ(T)) = 0, where Hⁿ = μHE[n] is applied as an outer measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (V T : Set (Rn n)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → T ⊆ V → volume T = 0 → μHE[n] (ψ '' T) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof Part 2, step 4 ("Lⁿ(T′) > 0 since Hⁿ(ψ(T′)) ≤ Lip(ψ|D)ⁿ Lⁿ(T′)"). This makes explicit the measure step that is implicit in Simon's proof of Lemma 3.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 490-492).

Notation. ℝ^d = Rn d. Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ. All measures are applied to arbitrary sets as outer measures.

Statement. Let n, N ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝⁿ open, ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ C¹ on V (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V), and T ⊆ V with Lⁿ(T) = 0. Then Hⁿ(ψ(T)) = 0.

Proof.

1. Facts about Hⁿ.
(a) μHE[n] = c_n · μH[n], where c_n := addHaarScalarFactor(volume on ℝⁿ, μH[n]) is a fixed element of ℝ≥0 (in particular finite) that does not depend on the ambient space (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def).
(b) If f is K-Lipschitz on a subset s of a metric space, then μH[n](f(s)) ≤ K^n μH[n](s) (LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le). Multiplying by c_n gives Hⁿ(f(s)) ≤ K^n Hⁿ(s).
(c) On ℝⁿ itself, Hⁿ = Lⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).

2. Local Lipschitz property. Let u ∈ T. Since u ∈ V and V is open, ψ is C¹ on a neighbourhood of u, so ψ is strictly differentiable at u (ContDiffAt.hasStrictFDerivAt). Hence ψ is Lipschitz on some neighbourhood t_u of u (HasStrictFDerivAt.exists_lipschitzOnWith; classically, apply the mean value inequality on a ball around u on which ‖Dψ‖ ≤ ‖Dψ(u)‖ + 1). That is, there is K_u ≥ 0 with |ψ(a) − ψ(b)| ≤ K_u |a − b| for all a, b ∈ t_u.

3. Local nullity. By 1(b) applied to the set T ∩ t_u ⊆ t_u, and 1(c):
Hⁿ(ψ(T ∩ t_u)) ≤ K_u^n Hⁿ(T ∩ t_u) = K_u^n Lⁿ(T ∩ t_u) ≤ K_u^n Lⁿ(T) = 0.

4. Countable cover. ℝⁿ is second countable, so (Lindelöf) a countable subfamily of the relative neighbourhoods T ∩ t_u (u ∈ T) covers T, say T ∩ t_{u_k} for k ∈ ℕ. Then ψ(T) = ⋃_k ψ(T ∩ t_{u_k}). By countable subadditivity of the outer measure Hⁿ, Hⁿ(ψ(T)) ≤ Σ_k Hⁿ(ψ(T ∩ t_{u_k})) = 0.
In Lean: apply measure_null_of_locally_null to the outer measure B ↦ μHE[n](ψ(B)) on ℝⁿ (OuterMeasure.comap ψ μHE[n], with comap_apply), using T ∩ t_u ∈ 𝓝[T] u. ∎

Remark. The case n = 0 is included: the argument applies verbatim, although Lⁿ(T) = 0 then already forces T = ∅. Measurability of T is never used.
proof_key_steps: Hⁿ = c_n·μH[n] with c_n a fixed finite constant; Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ; a K-Lipschitz map increases Hⁿ by at most a factor Kⁿ.
Each u ∈ T has a neighbourhood t_u on which ψ is Lipschitz, since C¹ near u implies strictly differentiable at u.
Hⁿ(ψ(T ∩ t_u)) ≤ K_uⁿ Lⁿ(T ∩ t_u) = 0.
By second countability, countably many t_u cover T; countable subadditivity gives Hⁿ(ψ(T)) = 0.

subproblems.title: Positive-measure chart pieces have a coordinate projection of positive measure
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝⁿ be open, and let ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ} be C¹ on V with Dψ(u) injective for every u ∈ V. If T ⊆ V has Lebesgue outer measure Lⁿ(T) > 0, then there is J ⊆ Fin(n+ℓ) with exactly n elements such that Hⁿ(coordinateProjection J (ψ(T))) > 0. Here Hⁿ = μHE[n] (outer measure), and coordinateProjection J is the orthogonal projection onto span{e_j : j ∈ J}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V T : Set (Rn n)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn (n + ℓ)), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → (∀ u ∈ V, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ u)) → T ⊆ V → 0 < volume T → ∃ J : Finset (Fin (n + ℓ)), J.card = n ∧ 0 < μHE[n] (coordinateProjection J '' (ψ '' T))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 3.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 492-496, printed p. 79, via Ch. 2, Remark 4.4); parent proof Part 2, steps 4-5 (density point and local bi-Lipschitz estimate).

Notation. ℝ^d = Rn d. Hⁿ = μHE[n] and Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, both outer measures. p_J := coordinateProjection J. Dψ(u) := fderiv ℝ ψ u.

Statement. Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝⁿ open, ψ C¹ on V with Dψ(u) injective for every u ∈ V, and T ⊆ V with Lⁿ(T) > 0. Then there is J ⊆ Fin(n+ℓ) with #J = n and Hⁿ(p_J(ψ(T))) > 0.

Proof.

1. Facts.
(a) μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n] with a fixed constant c_n ∈ ℝ≥0 (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def).
(b) Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
(c) If g : X → Y between metric spaces satisfies dist(x, y) ≤ K·dist(g(x), g(y)) for all x, y, then μH[n](s) ≤ K^n μH[n](g(s)) for every s ⊆ X (AntilipschitzWith.le_hausdorffMeasure_image).
(d) Hausdorff measure is intrinsic: for t ⊆ s ⊆ Z, μH[n](t) is the same whether computed in the metric subspace s or in Z (Isometry.hausdorffMeasure_image for the inclusion of s).

2. Density point (Simon line 492). There is u₀ ∈ T such that Lⁿ(T ∩ U) > 0 for every neighbourhood U of u₀. Otherwise every u ∈ T has a neighbourhood U_u with Lⁿ(T ∩ U_u) = 0. Since ℝⁿ is second countable, countably many U_u cover T, and countable subadditivity gives Lⁿ(T) = 0, a contradiction (Mathlib exists_mem_forall_mem_nhdsWithin_pos_measure).

3. Choice of J (sibling coordinate_projection_injective). Since u₀ ∈ T ⊆ V, D := Dψ(u₀) : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ} is injective, so L := D(ℝⁿ) has dim L = n (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj and dim ℝⁿ = n). The sibling, applied with N := n + ℓ and this L, gives J ⊆ Fin(n+ℓ) with #J = n such that p_J is injective on L.
Then A := p_J ∘ D : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ} is injective: if A v = A w, then p_J(Dv) = p_J(Dw) with Dv, Dw ∈ L, so Dv = Dw and v = w.

4. Lower bound for A. A is an injective linear map on the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ, so there is K > 0 with |v| ≤ K|Av| for all v ∈ ℝⁿ. For n ≥ 1 take K := 1/min_{|v|=1}|Av|, which is positive by compactness of the unit sphere and injectivity; for n = 0 any K > 0 works (Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith with ker A = 0).

5. Strict differentiability. This replaces the inverse function theorem in Simon's "C¹ diffeomorphism" step.
Put Φ := p_J ∘ ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ}. Since V is open, ψ is C¹ near u₀, hence strictly differentiable at u₀ with derivative D (ContDiffAt.hasStrictFDerivAt). Since p_J is continuous linear, Φ is strictly differentiable at u₀ with derivative A (chain rule).
Therefore there is a neighbourhood s of u₀ with |Φ(x) − Φ(y) − A(x − y)| ≤ (2K)⁻¹|x − y| for all x, y ∈ s (HasStrictFDerivAt.approximates_deriv_on_nhds with constant (2K)⁻¹ > 0).

6. Φ is anti-Lipschitz on s. For x, y ∈ s, by steps 4 and 5:
|x − y| ≤ K|A(x − y)| ≤ K(|Φ(x) − Φ(y)| + |Φ(x) − Φ(y) − A(x − y)|) ≤ K|Φ(x) − Φ(y)| + |x − y|/2.
Hence |x − y| ≤ 2K|Φ(x) − Φ(y)|.

7. Measure estimate. Let T' := T ∩ s. Since s is a neighbourhood of u₀, step 2 gives Lⁿ(T') > 0.
Apply fact (c) to the restriction g := Φ|_s : s → ℝ^{n+ℓ}, where s carries the induced metric and, by step 6, g satisfies the hypothesis with constant 2K. Apply it to T' ⊆ s, and use fact (d) to evaluate μH[n](T') in ℝⁿ. This gives μH[n](T') ≤ (2K)^n μH[n](Φ(T')). Multiplying by c_n: Hⁿ(T') ≤ (2K)^n Hⁿ(Φ(T')).
Since Hⁿ(T') = Lⁿ(T') > 0 by fact (b), and (2K)^n < ∞, we get Hⁿ(Φ(T')) > 0.
Equivalently, as in the parent proof: Φ|_s is injective with a 2K-Lipschitz inverse on Φ(s). The parent's further composition with the isometry ι_J⁻¹ : span{e_j : j ∈ J} → ℝⁿ changes no Hausdorff measure, so it is omitted.

8. Conclusion. Φ(T') = p_J(ψ(T')) ⊆ p_J(ψ(T)), so Hⁿ(p_J(ψ(T))) ≥ Hⁿ(Φ(T')) > 0, and #J = n. ∎

Remark. For n = 0 every step remains valid: T = {0}, L = 0, J = ∅, p_∅ = 0, and H⁰ is counting measure. Measurability of T is never used.
proof_key_steps: There is a density-type point u₀ ∈ T: every neighbourhood of u₀ meets T in positive Lebesgue outer measure.
The sibling coordinate_projection_injective, applied to L = range Dψ(u₀), gives J with #J = n such that A = p_J ∘ Dψ(u₀) is injective.
Injectivity gives |v| ≤ K|Av|. Strict differentiability of Φ = p_J ∘ ψ at u₀ gives |Φx − Φy − A(x−y)| ≤ |x−y|/(2K) on a neighbourhood s.
Hence |x − y| ≤ 2K|Φx − Φy| on s.
The anti-Lipschitz bound gives Hⁿ(T ∩ s) ≤ (2K)ⁿ Hⁿ(Φ(T ∩ s)). Since Hⁿ(T ∩ s) = Lⁿ(T ∩ s) > 0 and Φ(T ∩ s) ⊆ p_J(ψ(T)), the projection has positive measure.

subproblems.title: Lemma 3.3 (coordinate projection criterion), given Lemma 1.2
subproblems.statement: Assume Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 in the form SubmanifoldCoverCharacterization: for all n, ℓ and M ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}, M is countably n-rectifiable iff M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_j N_j with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 and each N_j an n-dimensional embedded C¹ submanifold (IsC1Submanifold n). Then Lemma 3.3 (CoordinateProjectionCriterion) holds: for all n, ℓ ∈ ℕ and S ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}, if Hⁿ(coordinateProjection J (S)) = 0 for every J ⊆ Fin(n+ℓ) with exactly n elements, then S is purely n-unrectifiable.
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, Lemma 3.3 and its proof (chapter-03.txt lines 476-496, printed pp. 78-79); parent proof Part 2, steps 2 and 4.
Erratum: Def. 3.1 (line 446) "if P contains" should read "if S contains". This is how the definition is encoded: PurelyUnrectifiable n S := ∀ R ⊆ S, CountablyRectifiable n R → Hⁿ(R) = 0.

Notation. ℝ^d = Rn d. Hⁿ = μHE[n] and Lⁿ = volume, both outer measures. p_J := coordinateProjection J.

Statement. Assume SubmanifoldCoverCharacterization (Lemma 1.2). Then for all n, ℓ and S ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with Hⁿ(p_J(S)) = 0 for every J with #J = n, S is purely n-unrectifiable.

Proof. Assume Lemma 1.2. Fix n, ℓ and S with the projection hypothesis
(H): Hⁿ(p_J(S)) = 0 whenever J ⊆ Fin(n+ℓ) and #J = n.
Let R ⊆ S be countably n-rectifiable; we show Hⁿ(R) = 0. Suppose instead that Hⁿ(R) ≠ 0.

1. Lemma 1.2, direction "⇒" (Simon line 490). Apply the assumed characterization to M := R. This gives N₀ ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 and sets N_j (j ∈ ℕ), each with IsC1Submanifold n N_j, such that R ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_j N_j.

2. Choice of a submanifold (Simon line 491). R ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_j (R ∩ N_j), so by countable subadditivity Hⁿ(R) ≤ Hⁿ(N₀) + Σ_j Hⁿ(R ∩ N_j) = Σ_j Hⁿ(R ∩ N_j). Since Hⁿ(R) ≠ 0, some j has Hⁿ(R ∩ N_j) ≠ 0. Fix it and write N := N_j.

3. Charts. By IsC1Submanifold n N, each y ∈ N has:
- an open set V_y ⊆ ℝⁿ;
- an open set W_y ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with y ∈ W_y;
- a map ψ_y : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ}, C¹ on V_y, with Dψ_y(u) injective for all u ∈ V_y and ψ_y(V_y) = W_y ∩ N.
Injectivity and properness of ψ_y are not needed.
The open sets W_y (y ∈ N) cover N. Since ℝ^{n+ℓ} is second countable, there is a countable I ⊆ N with ⋃_{y∈I} W_y = ⋃_{y∈N} W_y ⊇ N (Lindelöf; Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable).

4. Choice of a chart. R ∩ N ⊆ ⋃_{y∈I} (R ∩ N ∩ W_y), so countable subadditivity gives y ∈ I with Hⁿ(R ∩ N ∩ W_y) ≠ 0. Write V := V_y and ψ := ψ_y.

5. Let T := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(R) ⊆ V. Then ψ(T) = ψ(V) ∩ R = W_y ∩ N ∩ R, so Hⁿ(ψ(T)) ≠ 0.

6. Apply the sibling c1_image_null with N := n + ℓ, V, T and ψ (V is open, ψ is C¹ on V, T ⊆ V). If Lⁿ(T) = 0, it would give Hⁿ(ψ(T)) = 0. Hence Lⁿ(T) > 0.

7. Apply the sibling chart_projection_positive to n, ℓ, V, T and ψ (Dψ(u) is injective for u ∈ V). It gives J ⊆ Fin(n+ℓ) with #J = n and Hⁿ(p_J(ψ(T))) > 0. This is Simon lines 492-496: near a density point the coordinate projection is bi-Lipschitz on the chart image, so the projection of S ∩ N has positive measure.

8. Since ψ(T) ⊆ R ⊆ S, we have p_J(ψ(T)) ⊆ p_J(S). So Hⁿ(p_J(S)) ≥ Hⁿ(p_J(ψ(T))) > 0, contradicting (H) for this J. Therefore Hⁿ(R) = 0. As R ⊆ S was an arbitrary countably n-rectifiable set, S is purely n-unrectifiable. ∎

Remarks.
- Only the forward direction of Lemma 1.2 is used.
- No measurability of S or R is needed; all estimates use outer measure.
- The argument is uniform in n. For n = 0 one can also argue directly, as in the parent proof: J = ∅ gives p_∅(S) = {0}, of H⁰-measure 1 unless S = ∅.
proof_key_steps: Suppose R ⊆ S is countably rectifiable with Hⁿ(R) ≠ 0. Lemma 1.2 (⇒) covers R by a null set N₀ and C¹ submanifolds N_j.
Countable subadditivity gives j with Hⁿ(R ∩ N_j) ≠ 0. Lindelöf on the chart domains W_y then gives a chart (V, W, ψ) with Hⁿ(R ∩ N_j ∩ W) ≠ 0.
T := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(R) satisfies ψ(T) = R ∩ N_j ∩ W, so Lⁿ(T) > 0 by the sibling c1_image_null.
The sibling chart_projection_positive gives J with #J = n and Hⁿ(p_J(ψ(T))) > 0. But p_J(ψ(T)) ⊆ p_J(S), which is Hⁿ-null — a contradiction.

subproblems.title: Theorem 3.8 (rectifiability theorem for sets), given Theorem 3.6
subproblems.statement: Assume Simon Ch. 3, Theorem 3.6 in the form BesicovitchFedererProjectionTheorem: for all n, ℓ and every purely n-unrectifiable Q ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with Q = ⋃_j Q_j and Hⁿ(Q_j) < ∞, ForAlmostAllProjections (n+ℓ) n (p ↦ Hⁿ(p(Q)) = 0). Then Theorem 3.8 (RectifiabilityTheoremForSets) holds. That is, let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ and A ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with A = ⋃_j A_j and Hⁿ(A_j) < ∞, and suppose every B ⊆ A with Hⁿ(B) > 0 satisfies ¬ForAlmostAllProjections (n+ℓ) n (p ↦ Hⁿ(p(B)) = 0). Then A is countably n-rectifiable.
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, Theorem 3.8 and the sentence preceding it (chapter-03.txt lines 535-548, printed p. 80); parent proof Part 3, step 6.
Erratum: line 540 "by combining 3.2 and 3.7" should read "by combining 3.2 and 3.6". Remark 3.7 is the converse direction, while the argument uses the null-projection Theorem 3.6, which is the hypothesis BesicovitchFedererProjectionTheorem here.

Notation. ℝ^d = Rn d. Hⁿ = μHE[n], an outer measure.

Statement. Assume BesicovitchFedererProjectionTheorem. Then RectifiabilityTheoremForSets holds.

Proof. Assume Theorem 3.6. Fix n, ℓ, A and (A_j) with A = ⋃_j A_j and Hⁿ(A_j) < ∞, together with the hypothesis
(P): for every B ⊆ A with 0 < Hⁿ(B), ¬ForAlmostAllProjections (n+ℓ) n (p ↦ Hⁿ(p(B)) = 0).

1. Apply the sibling rectifiable_decomposition (Lemma 3.2, first conclusion) to A with the same A_j. This gives A = R ∪ P with R countably n-rectifiable and P purely n-unrectifiable; disjointness is not needed.

2. P ⊆ R ∪ P = A. For j ∈ ℕ put P_j := P ∩ A_j. Since P ⊆ A = ⋃_j A_j, we have P = ⋃_j P_j, and Hⁿ(P_j) ≤ Hⁿ(A_j) < ∞ by monotonicity.

3. Theorem 3.6 applied to Q := P (purely n-unrectifiable) with Q_j := P_j gives ForAlmostAllProjections (n+ℓ) n (p ↦ Hⁿ(p(P)) = 0).

4. If Hⁿ(P) > 0, then (P) with B := P (allowed since P ⊆ A) gives ¬ForAlmostAllProjections (n+ℓ) n (p ↦ Hⁿ(p(P)) = 0), contradicting step 3. Hence Hⁿ(P) = 0.

5. Since R is countably n-rectifiable, there are M₀ with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ} (k ∈ ℕ) with R ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_k F_k(ℝⁿ). Then A = R ∪ P ⊆ (M₀ ∪ P) ∪ ⋃_k F_k(ℝⁿ), and Hⁿ(M₀ ∪ P) ≤ Hⁿ(M₀) + Hⁿ(P) = 0. This is exactly Definition 1.1 for A, with exceptional set M₀ ∪ P and the same maps F_k. So A is countably n-rectifiable. ∎

Remark. In the parent node, the hypothesis is discharged by the declared dependency Submission.besicovitchFedererProjectionTheorem_holds (node root.besicovitch_federer-a1).
proof_key_steps: Lemma 3.2 (sibling rectifiable_decomposition) gives A = R ∪ P with R countably rectifiable and P purely unrectifiable.
P = ⋃_j (P ∩ A_j) with Hⁿ(P ∩ A_j) < ∞, so Theorem 3.6 (the hypothesis) gives null projections of P for almost all projections.
The hypothesis on positive-measure subsets of A, applied with B := P, forces Hⁿ(P) = 0.
Absorb P into the null exceptional set of R's Lipschitz cover; hence A is countably n-rectifiable.
